details: The European Central Bank (ECB) is widely anticipated to implement two interest rate hikes in 2026, with the first 25 basis point increase expected as early as June. This shift towards tighter monetary policy, a reversal from previous easing expectations, is driven by accelerating Eurozone inflation, which reached 3.2% in May, exceeding the ECB's 2% target. Higher interest rates typically reduce the attractiveness of riskier assets like cryptocurrencies, as investors can find more appealing returns in traditional, safer euro-denominated investments.
title: ECB Poised for Multiple Rate Hikes Amid Accelerating Inflation

details: The cryptocurrency market is closely watching two major macroeconomic events in the coming week: the release of US May Consumer Price Index (CPI) data on June 10 and the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on June 17. A "hot" CPI reading, especially above 3.6% year-over-year, could diminish the likelihood of any 2026 rate cuts by the Federal Reserve, strengthening the US Dollar Index (DXY) and potentially leading to a significant test of Bitcoin's mid-$60,000 support levels. Conversely, a cooler inflation print could offer some relief to crypto markets.
title: Upcoming US CPI and FOMC Meetings to Dictate Bitcoin's Trajectory

details: The US Treasury is expanding its sanctions against Iran, now targeting Nobitex, Iran's largest cryptocurrency exchange. This move is part of an escalating effort to disrupt the financial infrastructure Tehran uses to operate outside the traditional banking system and facilitate illicit activities. The sanctions underscore a growing focus by global regulators on the use of cryptocurrencies for sanctions evasion, increasing the regulatory risk profile for the broader crypto market.
title: US Escalates Sanctions on Iran, Targets Crypto Exchange

details: Bitcoin has seen a significant pullback, marked by 12 consecutive sessions of net outflows from US spot Bitcoin ETFs, representing the longest such streak since their launch and the largest monthly exodus of 2026. This trend suggests a shift in investor sentiment, as capital is rotating away from cryptocurrencies towards traditional equity markets, particularly artificial intelligence (AI) and technology stocks, which are perceived to offer stronger momentum and clearer growth narratives. The Crypto Fear and Greed Index has also moved deeper into "fear" territory.
title: Bitcoin Experiences Prolonged ETF Outflows as Capital Shifts to Equities
